b2-113.title: A health talk at school
b2-113.story: On Friday, a school nurse came to Anna's class to give a health talk. She started with [[nicotine]] and explained how quickly young people become addicted to it. Then she talked about harder drugs like [[cocaine]] and [[heroin]], which can destroy a life in a few months. Someone asked whether [[marijuana]] is safe, since it is legal in some countries. The nurse said it can still harm a teenage brain. She told them about a young man who spent a year in [[rehab]] before he finally got better. "For him, stress was the main [[trigger]]," she said, "so he learned new ways to relax." The second part of the talk was about the body and safe relationships, and she explained what a [[condom]] is and how it protects against infections. She even used a simple diagram of the [[penis]], and Max turned bright red. Afterward, Anna told him it was useful information, and he finally agreed.

b2-114.title: A visit to the clinic
b2-114.story: On Saturday morning, Anna took Taras to the clinic for his yearly [[checkup]]. Half the waiting room was coughing, because [[influenza]] was going around the city. The nurse put a [[thermometer]] under Taras's arm and said his temperature was normal. Taras admitted he never used [[floss]], so the doctor showed him how to clean between his teeth. Anna asked about her [[acne]], and the doctor recommended a gentle face wash. Their mama had come along too, because she wanted advice about the [[migraine]] she gets every few weeks. Their dad was there for a blood test, since the doctor wanted to check his [[cholesterol]] again. In the restroom, Anna noticed a basket of free pads and [[tampons|tampon]], which she thought was a kind idea. On the way home, Taras proudly showed everyone the sticker the doctor had given him.

b2-115.title: The ambulance night shift
b2-115.story: Max's sister Sofia works as a [[paramedic]] in Kyiv, and last week Max joined her for part of a night shift. At the station, the [[dispatcher]] sat in front of three screens and answered every call calmly. Sofia's partner, a former army [[medic]], drove the ambulance. Around midnight, Sofia's [[pager]] beeped, and they rushed to an elderly man with chest pain. She connected him to a heart monitor and explained that he needed constant [[monitoring]] on the way to the hospital. His wife mentioned nervously that he'd had [[laser]] surgery on his eyes a month earlier, so Sofia wrote that down too. On the drive back, she told Max about the [[lockdown]] in 2020, when the ambulances almost never stopped. Max had expected excitement, but mostly he saw tired people doing careful work. At six in the morning, Sofia bought him a coffee and said he had survived his first shift.

b2-116.title: A hard road back
b2-116.story: Ira's uncle Bohdan used to be a popular local football coach, until [[alcoholism]] slowly took away his job and his friends. For years he refused to admit that he was an [[alcoholic]]. Last winter, he finally went to a hospital for a week-long [[detox]], and Ira visited him every Sunday. He told her that the hardest part was a strange [[phobia]] of crowded rooms that he had developed while drinking. Little by little, he started going to support meetings and walking in the park every morning. In spring, a youth team asked him to help with training. On the field, he still moved by [[instinct]], shouting to the boys before they even saw the danger. In his first match, his team was losing 0–2 but made an amazing [[comeback]] and won 3–2. Ira and her friends cheered louder than anyone in the stands.

b2-117.title: Grandpa and Grandma's checkup
b2-117.story: Anna went with her grandparents to their family doctor, because both of them had a long list of questions. Grandpa started by complaining about a slight [[tremor]] in his hands. The doctor tested the [[reflex]] in his knee with a little hammer, and everything looked normal. Grandma had suffered from [[diarrhea]] for two days after a picnic, and the doctor suspected [[salmonella]] from the chicken salad. She didn't need an [[antibiotic]], just plenty of water and rest. Then Grandpa mentioned that he was allergic to [[penicillin]], so the doctor added a warning to his file. Anna asked whether [[zinc]] really helps against colds, and the doctor said it can, in small amounts. She also renewed the inhaler prescription for Taras, whose [[asthma]] gets worse in spring. Finally, Grandma proudly said she remembered getting the [[polio]] vaccine as a little girl. On the way out, Grandpa joked that he felt healthier just from talking about it.

b2-118.title: In the hospital lab
b2-118.story: Anna's biology class visited the lab at a big hospital in Kyiv. A friendly scientist let each student look at a drop of pond water under a [[microscope]]. Lisa was the first to spot an [[amoeba]], slowly changing its shape as it moved. The scientist explained that every [[microorganism]] in the drop was alive, even though none of them could be seen with the naked eye. "Not every [[microbe]] is dangerous," she added, "and many of them keep us healthy." Next, she showed them a [[tumor]] that a surgeon had removed that morning, and said that luckily it wasn't cancer. Max asked whether she had ever used a [[scalpel]], and she laughed and said only in medical school. She also told them about a boy whose [[appendix]] was removed last week and who was now recovering well. Before they left, she mentioned that the hospital runs a small [[hospice]] next door, where volunteers read to patients. Ira decided right there that she wanted to become one of those volunteers.

b2-119.title: At the pharmacy
b2-119.story: After a weekend at the lake, Lisa and Ira stopped at the pharmacy with a long list. Lisa had a bad sunburn, so the pharmacist gave her a bottle of cooling [[aloe vera]] gel. Ira laughed and said her grandma just cuts a leaf from the [[aloe]] on her windowsill. Ira had a headache, and the pharmacist suggested [[paracetamol]] because her stomach was already upset. "Don't take [[ibuprofen]] on an empty stomach," she warned. Lisa also needed some [[antiseptic]] for a cut on her foot from a sharp rock. Ira grabbed a small tin of [[vaseline]] for her dry lips. The pharmacist recommended a [[probiotic]] for Ira's stomach and asked whether she had eaten anything unusual. Ira admitted she had eaten a whole bag of peanuts, and the pharmacist joked that at least they weren't an [[allergen]] for her. The girls walked out laughing and promised to wear sunscreen next time.

b2-120.title: The doctor's advice
b2-120.story: Before visiting her grandparents, Anna woke up with a sore throat and took an [[antigen test]] just in case. It was negative, but she still went to see the family doctor with Max. The doctor said it was probably a cold, not the [[coronavirus]], and checked that Anna had had her [[diphtheria]] shot. Then she noticed that Anna's dad, who had driven them there, had paint on his hands. She told him to wear a [[respirator]] while he painted the kitchen. Max admitted that he had tried his cousin's [[vape]] at a party. The doctor didn't lecture him, but explained that [[vaping]] can damage young lungs and is hard to quit. In the hallway, Anna noticed a poster about free support for teens with [[bulimia]] and saved the phone number, just in case a friend ever needed it. On the way home, Max said he was glad he had only tried it once.
